subject: Zero-Trust Outbound Policy for Private Connectors
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <a.khan@acme-fintech.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private connector egress / allowlist questions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week — we're beginning the internal network review for Acme's on-prem Private Connector (air-gapped rack in our primary data center). Security has a few follow-ups before we can sign off on the PoC. Can you confirm the definitive list of outbound hosts (domain names and/or IPs) and the minimal set of protocols/ports we should allow?

Specific asks:
- Explicit hostnames (control plane, artifact mirrors) and whether those resolve to stable IPs we can allowlist.
- Whether Redwood can operate entirely over HTTPS (443) or if additional ports are required.
- Support for customer egress proxies (we have a corporate forward proxy + TLS intercept) — will that break model pulls or websocket/streaming connections?
- Logging/audit expectations: which events are emitted from the connector versus the control plane, and where do logs go?

We're on a tight timeline to get the connector in the DMZ next week, so a short bulleted summary would help.

Appreciate it —
Aisha
Aisha Khan
Head of Security Engineering, Acme Fintech
security@acme-fintech.com

Attachments: none

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <a.khan@acme-fintech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private connector egress / allowlist questions

Aisha —

Thanks for the questions. Below is a concise, implementation-oriented summary you can hand to your network team. I've attached a short spec PDF for clipboard-friendly copy/paste (redwood-private-connectors-egress-safelist.pdf).

High-level: Redwood's Private Connector establishes outbound-only HTTPS connections from your connector(s) to our control endpoints and to artifact mirrors. We recommend a zero-trust outbound posture with strict allowlisting by FQDN and (if required by policy) by the static egress IPs below.

Minimum outbound allowances (recommended):
- Protocol: HTTPS (TLS 1.2+). Ports: 443 (required).
- DNS: Allow your resolver to resolve our FQDNs; block direct external DNS to avoid exfil.
- Control plane FQDNs: control.redwood.ai, auth-us1.redwood.ai, metrics.redwood.ai
- Artifact mirrors (pulls, model shards): mirrors.redwood.ai (resolves to regional pools; see PDF).
- Optional monitoring: outbound syslog/metrics over TLS to your centralized collector (if you use a dedicated egress gateway).

Static egress IPs (for allowlisting when egress IPs are mandated) — note these are regional and subject to change; prefer FQDN allowlisting when possible:
- us-west: 52.23.140.0/24
- us-east: 34.210.128.0/24
- eu-west: 18.194.60.0/24

Important operational notes:
- Websocket streaming is tunneled over HTTPS using standard Upgrade semantics; nothing outside 443 is required.
- mTLS to the control plane is supported (mutual auth) for enterprise customers — we can provide cert provisioning guidance if you require it.
- Artifact downloads may be large. If you have an egress gateway with static NAT IPs, point the connector's artifact cache to that gateway to keep flows consistent.
- If your proxy performs TLS MITM with custom roots, ensure the connector trusts the proxy root or use an egress gateway with certificate passthrough.

Logs & auditing:
- Connector emits local audit logs for request metadata, cache hits/misses, and connectivity events.
- Control plane emits delivery/upgrade events and token exchange traces (redacted).
- We recommend centralizing connector logs to your SIEM over TLS with structured JSON; retention 90 days is typical for initial deployments.

Next steps:
1) Review attached PDF and confirm if your policy requires IP-only allowlist (we can provide a signed IP range list).
2) Let's do a short technical call Tue Jan 12 to walk the ops team through a sample firewall config.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-private-connectors-egress-safelist.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

On Sun, Jan 10, 2027 at 10:45 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Aisha —
> 
> Thanks for the questions. Below is a concise, implementation-oriented summary you can hand to your network team. I've attached a short spec PDF for clipboard-friendly copy/paste (redwood-private-connectors-egress-safelist.pdf).

Quick firewall recipe (example for a perimeter appliance):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to: control.redwood.ai, auth-us1.redwood.ai, mirrors.redwood.ai (FQDN allowlist preferred).
- Deny all other outbound to internet from connector VLAN/subnet.
- Allow outbound DNS only to your enterprise resolvers (do NOT allow public 8.8.8.8/1.1.1.1 from the connector).
- If you use an egress gateway with static IPs, allow 52.23.140.0/24 and 34.210.128.0/24 for initial rollout. Add eu range if deploying in EU.

Sample iptables-ish ACL (pseudocode):
- iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -d <control.redwood.ai IPs> -j ACCEPT
- iptables -A OUTPUT -p udp --dport 53 -d <enterprise-dns> -j ACCEPT
- iptables -A OUTPUT -j DROP

DNS & exfil protection:
- Enforce DNS resolution through your internal resolvers; enable response buffering/inspection to catch suspicious TXT/URL responses.
- Optionally pin control plane hostnames in /etc/hosts for initial validation, but switch to resolver-based once cert validation is confirmed.

Artifact caching & NAT behavior:
- Connector performs model shard downloads during warm-up. Large pulls should traverse your egress gateway to avoid dynamic ephemeral NAT.
- For HA: configure a dedicated egress profile for connector subnets so NAT does not rotate across many IPs.

Logging & replay:
- Export connector audit lines (timestamp, request_id, fqn, bytes_transferred, cache_status) to your SIEM over TLS.
- We recommend 90–180 day retention during the PoC.

I've attached a small CSV that maps ports/purpose (connector-port-matrix.csv). Happy to walk through during the call.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

- We'll route connector traffic through our egress gateway so NAT IPs remain static for auditing.
- We'll ship the initial logs to our SIEM (TLS endpoint) and keep 90 days retention for PoC.
